purpose: Align API layers with engineering responsibilities, OS primitives and a symbolic topology vocabulary so agents can reason across abstraction levels without treating analogy as authority.
guardrails: Symbolic mapping is a cognitive alignment aid, not an authority layer.
Executable contracts, runtime evidence and validators outrank symbolic analogy.
Do not infer religious meaning into protocol behavior, security policy or deployment authorization.
When analogy and engineering evidence disagree, update or discard the analogy.

symbolic_vocabulary.Keter: objective, source intent and organism purpose
symbolic_vocabulary.Chokhmah: generative insight, candidate hypothesis and raw novelty
symbolic_vocabulary.Binah: structure, contract, schema and bounded form
symbolic_vocabulary.Chesed: expansion, capacity, delegation and resource generosity
symbolic_vocabulary.Gevurah: constraint, security, rate limit, claim and refusal
symbolic_vocabulary.Tiferet: integration, judgement, routing and balanced decision
symbolic_vocabulary.Hod: protocol, language, interface and formal adapter
symbolic_vocabulary.Yesod: transmission, state bridge, queue and durable foundation
symbolic_vocabulary.Malkhut: manifest runtime surface, process, file, socket and user-visible effect

perception.engineering_role: Observe and expose current organism state without owning mutation.
must: Return current evidence instead of desired state.
Remain agent-safe by default unless the endpoint leaks sensitive data.
must_not: Become the source of truth for policy.

memory.engineering_role: Persist observations, tasks, crystals and read-back proof.
must: Provide durable read-back for mempool writes.
Separate committed memory from transient runtime effects.
must_not: Hide irreversible runtime mutation behind a memory verb.
Store volatile runtime snapshots as source-of-truth code.

coordination.engineering_role: Coordinate actors, claims, leases, sessions and contention boundaries.
coordination.agent_question: Who may act on this resource?
must: Represent claims as bounded runtime facts.
Expose who/claim/release style introspection for agents.
must_not: Deploy, provision or restore infrastructure directly.
Pretend stale static claims outrank live kernel state.

cognition.engineering_role: Judge, route, score and infer without directly owning deployment mutation.
cognition.agent_question: What should be inferred or decided?
must: Separate inference requests from infrastructure activation.
Expose status/read paths for async decisions.
must_not: Start or remediate runtime processes under a cognition-only route.
Conflate verdict production with deployment authority.

metabolism.engineering_role: Change organism runtime: deploy, provision, restore, backup, start, remediate or send side-effectful work.
metabolism.agent_question: What is the organism changing in its body?
must: Require explicit lifecycle authorization for deployment or destructive mutation.
Use registry-driven targets for build and runtime placement.
Expose dangerous operations as not agent-safe by default.
must_not: Run canonical release builds from cortex-local state.
Hide deployment, restore or destructive effects behind coordination or perception roots.

compatibility.engineering_role: Adapt external protocols and legacy clients while pointing to canonical organism families.
compatibility.agent_question: Which foreign or legacy shape is being translated?
must: Declare the canonical family for every compatibility operation.
Preserve external interoperability without becoming policy source of truth.
Carry deprecation or compatibility status in machine-readable contracts.
must_not: Outlive its canonical replacement without an explicit reason.
Invent a parallel ontology for the same organism capability.

vertical_alignment_rules.rule: deployment operations must be metabolism or must name a canonical lifecycle family; destructive resource operations may stay in their owning layer but must never be agent_safe_default.
perception operations must use read or stream mutation levels unless they are explicitly recording external events into the mempool or registering runtime presence.
compatibility and transitional operations must point at a distinct canonical family.
mempool writes that create durable memory must have a read-back family in the API topology.
deployment and destructive lifecycle operations must not be agent_safe_default.
